- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecasted values by 5–10% to account for bearish sentiment bias.  
- If recent price action shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak by 5–15% and smooth the decline.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is trending downward, increase forecasted values by 5–10% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- Model often underestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 day) horizons — adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed, avoid sharp directional forecasts — use 3–5% buffer around mean of recent 7-day range.  
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in 30-day horizon when sentiment is consistently negative — apply a 3–7% downward bias to correct for pessimism.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is near recent high, model tends to overestimate — reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overbought bias.
